subject: Customer questions: storage sovereignty and deletion proof for Private/VPC deployment
messages:
From: Liang Chen <liang.chen@valianthealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: privacy@valianthealth.com
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions about data residency & deletion for Private (VPC) deployment

Hi Marissa,

We're preparing to onboard Redwood Private into our AWS account and the security/privacy team has a few specific requirements we need to satisfy before procurement: 

1) We need guarantees that all customer content (prompts, responses, embeddings, and any generated artifacts) will reside only in customer-controlled storage in our AWS account — not copied to Redwood-managed S3 or backups in other regions.
2) We need a documented deletion workflow and a way to obtain verifiable proof of deletion (manifest, signed CloudTrail events, object delete markers) when we ask for a purge.
3) Do system snapshots, model cache checkpoints, or debug traces ever persist outside our VPC or customer bucket (for example, pushed into Redwood telemetry or backups)?
4) What about ephemeral data like KV cache, GPU memory; and secondary telemetry (usage metering, latency logs) — are those optional to disable or can they be configured to anonymize and store only in our account?

Can you point us to the most up-to-date runbook and provide an outline we can use in our internal risk review? We will need this info for our SOC-2 readiness checklist and to confirm data residency for EU/US workloads.

Thanks,
Liang
Security & Privacy, Valiant Health

Hi Liang — thanks for the clear list. I've looped in Karthik (security/infra) and Vivek (solutions) to confirm the technical details; attaching a high-level VPC data flow and a short deletion checklist so your reviewers have something tangible.

High level: Redwood Private is designed so customer content can remain only in customer-controlled storage. That said, there are configuration options with different trade-offs (control plane telemetry vs. fully air-gapped). Karthik and Vivek will outline the default behaviors and the stronger configuration (no control-plane artifacts) and the steps we take to produce deletion evidence.

Quick questions for your team so we provide the right artifacts:
- Will you be using an S3 bucket in the same account as the deployment, or do you prefer a cross-account bucket?
- Do you require us to disable all control-plane telemetry or is anonymized usage metrics acceptable?

I'll follow up with a technical annex once Karthik confirms. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with your security folks early next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Karhik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Questions about data residency & deletion for Private (VPC) deployment

Marissa / team — writing up the specifics. Short answers first, then a concise checklist you can share with the customer.

Short answers:
- Customer content (user payloads, embeddings, model outputs) can be configured to remain exclusively in the customer's S3/GCS bucket in their AWS/GCP account. We support two deployment topologies:
  * Data-plane-only (recommended for maximum sovereignty): model artifacts and customer objects live only in customer buckets or local disks in their VPC; control plane has no access to object contents.
  * Hybrid (default on trial): control plane receives minimal metadata for routing/health; all raw content is written to customer storage.

- Backups/snapshots:
  * Point-in-time snapshots of persistent stores are written to a customer-configured snapshot bucket in the same account by default. Cross-account replication is disabled unless you ask us to set it up.
  * Automated daily backups can be turned off; we can schedule them to use lifecycle rules (e.g., 7-day retention then auto-delete).

- KV caches and GPU state:
  * KV caches are in-process (GPU/instance memory) and are ephemeral. Persisted checkpoints are optional and only written to the customer bucket if snapshotting is enabled.

- Telemetry & logs:
  * Usage telemetry (token counts, per-request latency) is configurable: default collects anonymized metrics in the control plane for billing/observability. You can disable or limit telemetry and export raw logs to your CloudWatch/Stackdriver endpoint instead.
  * Audit logs (control-plane auth events, admin actions) can be configured to be exported to your account using CloudTrail/EventBridge connectors.

Verifiable deletion proof (what we can provide):
1) Manifest of deleted objects (list of S3 keys + sizes) with a deletion timestamp.
2) Signed CloudTrail/CloudWatch logs showing DeleteObject/DeleteObjects API calls (these include request IDs).
3) S3 delete markers / Object version garbage-collection confirmation when versioning is enabled.
4) KMS key rotation / scheduled key destruction record if you require crypto-proof of unreadability.

Checklist to share with customer (short):
- Deploy Redwood Private data plane into customer's account with customer-provided S3 bucket and KMS keys.
- Configure snapshots to write to the same account; disable cross-account replication.
- Set object lifecycle policies (e.g., 90-day retention) as required by customer policy.
- Disable any control-plane telemetry collection (if required) and enable event export to customer's CloudTrail.
- At deletion request: trigger deletion job, generate manifest, export CloudTrail range for deletion events, provide signed manifest and optionally rotate/destroy KMS keys.

Notes / caveats:
- Some debug-level traces (if enabled) may be stored temporarily in the control plane unless explicitly disabled. We recommend disabling debug traces for regulated workloads.
- Immutable model artifacts (open-source weights) are not considered customer data; we do not write customer prompts to model weight storage.

I'll drop a plain-text checklist and a sample manifest template in the shared drive link and copy you when that's ready.

—Kar

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Questions about data residency & deletion for Private (VPC) deployment

Hi Liang — thanks for the patience. Below is a concise, shareable summary you can take to your security and procurement teams; fully backed by our engineers.

Summary (what we will guarantee for a Redwood Private deployment in your AWS account):
- Residency: All customer content (inputs, outputs, embeddings) will be stored only in your customer-managed S3 buckets in the same AWS account and region you specify. We will not copy raw customer content to Redwood-managed buckets.
- Backups & snapshots: Snapshots are written to a customer-configured snapshot bucket in your account. Cross-account replication and Redwood-managed snapshot copies are not created by default.
- Ephemeral state: KV caches live in GPU/instance memory and are not persisted unless you opt into checkpointing; any persisted checkpoint is written to your bucket.
- Telemetry & logs: Collection is configurable. By default we collect anonymized usage metrics in our control plane for billing; you can disable that and export required logs/metrics directly to your CloudWatch.
- Deletion proof: Upon a deletion request we will run the deletion workflow and provide:
  * A deletion manifest (S3 key list + delete timestamps),
  * Signed CloudTrail export showing DeleteObject requests,
  * Optional proof of KMS key rotation/destruction if you require crypto-proof.

Next steps we propose:
1) Confirm which S3 bucket (account/ARN) Redwood should write to.
2) Tell us whether to disable control-plane telemetry and debug traces.
3) If you want, schedule a 30-minute technical call this Thursday/Friday for a run-through of the deletion workflow and to hand over the manifest template.

I have uploaded the technical annex and manifest template to a shared drive (link below) and attached the flow diagram/checklist again for convenience.
